The ordered sequence of agent decisions, tool calls, observations and state transitions.
Whether the agent selected the correct tool and supplied valid arguments for the task.
Whether claims are supported by retrieved evidence and citations.

explanation.problem: An agent can sound convincing while calling the wrong tool, leaking another tenant's data, inventing citations, ignoring approval policy or consuming an excessive budget. Unit tests for individual functions do not reveal these trajectory-level failures. Agent systems need repeatable evaluation across outcomes, decisions, safety and operations.
explanation.plainLanguage:
Start by defining what success means for one task. A support agent may need to identify the right order, call order_lookup and policy_search, cite the correct policy and request human approval before a high-value refund. A plausible paragraph alone is not success. Define expected final behavior, allowed tools, argument constraints, required evidence, forbidden actions and resource budgets.

Build a golden dataset with ordinary cases, edge cases, adversarial prompts, ambiguous requests, tool failures, stale data, cross-tenant attempts and approval scenarios. Version the dataset and preserve the exact configuration used for every run. Keep training or prompt-development examples separate from held-out evaluation cases to avoid tuning directly to the test set.

Evaluate multiple layers. Task success asks whether the user goal was completed. Tool evaluation checks selected tool, arguments, order and unnecessary calls. Grounding checks whether citations point to the right source and whether claims are supported. Trajectory evaluation checks the full sequence: did the agent recover from an error, stop at the right time and avoid repeating side effects? Safety evaluation checks permissions, tenant isolation, policy compliance and approval. Operational evaluation measures latency, token use, cost, retries and timeouts.

Use deterministic assertions wherever possible: exact tool names, tenant IDs, required approval flags, citation IDs, maximum call counts and forbidden actions. For subjective quality, use human review or a calibrated model-based judge, but validate the judge against a human-labeled sample. A judge model can share the same blind spots as the agent. Do not let an LLM judge replace security tests.

Separate hard gates from weighted scores. A candidate that leaks data or executes a refund without approval is rejected even if its answer quality and latency are excellent. After all hard gates pass, calculate a weighted score for task success, grounding, trajectory, latency and cost. Report per-dimension metrics and confidence/variance, not just one aggregate number.

Run evaluations across repeated trials when model output is stochastic. Report sample size, mean and variance, and p50/p95 latency. Compare candidate changes against a pinned baseline and alert on meaningful regressions. Preserve redacted traces so failures can be diagnosed. Store candidate version, prompt version, model ID, tool schema version, dataset hash and configuration hash with every run.

Evaluation is continuous. Use offline golden tests before release, shadow evaluation on representative production traffic, canary rollout with rollback thresholds and periodic human review. Production data needs consent, minimization, retention and redaction controls. An evaluation suite measures known risks; it cannot prove that an agent is safe in every possible context.
explanation.mentalModel: Define expected behavior → build versioned cases → capture full trajectory → score quality and operations → enforce hard safety gates → compare against baseline → improve and rerun.
limitations: Golden datasets cannot cover every real-world prompt or environment change.
Model-based judges can be biased and must be calibrated against human labels.
A high average score can hide rare but severe safety failures; inspect slices and hard gates.
Stochastic models require repeated trials and uncertainty reporting.
Production traces may contain personal or confidential data; redact and govern retention.
Evaluation metrics can be gamed if prompts are overfit to the benchmark.
explanation.everydayAnalogy: A driving test does not grade only whether the car reaches the destination. It also checks lane discipline, signals, braking, hazard response and time. Agent evaluation works the same way: inspect the outcome and the decisions taken along the route.
explanation.mathMadeSimple: Suppose 100 test tasks produce 92 successful outcomes, 96 correct tool selections, 88 grounded answers and 95 safe trajectories. Task success rate is 92/100=92%; tool accuracy is 96%; groundedness pass rate is 88%; safety pass rate is 95%. If one of the five safety failures is cross-tenant data access, the candidate fails the hard safety gate even though its weighted average is high. For latency samples sorted ascending, P50 is the middle observation and P95 is near the 95th percentile; P95 reveals slow tail cases hidden by the mean.
explanation.productionImpact: Production evaluation needs versioned datasets, deterministic and human-judged checks, adversarial slices, trace redaction, pinned model/tool/prompt configuration, repeated trials, confidence intervals, p50/p95 latency, cost attribution, release gates, canary thresholds and rollback automation.

useCase.scenario: Evaluate an ecommerce support agent on refund eligibility. The dataset includes valid refunds, missing citations, wrong tool calls, cross-tenant attempts, high-value approval and provider timeout cases. A candidate must pass every safety gate before quality score is considered.
inputs: Allowed tool registry and tenant policy
constraints: Same dataset and configuration for baseline and candidate.
No cross-tenant access or unauthorized side effect.
Missing evidence is not counted as grounded.
Hard safety failures reject regardless of aggregate score.
outputs: Per-case task, tool, grounding and safety metrics
useCase.successMetric: A release candidate passes all critical safety gates and meets task-quality, grounding, latency and cost thresholds on held-out cases.

dataFlow.purpose: Score task, tool, grounding and policy behavior.
Reject safety regressions and gate rollout.

trustBoundaries: Evaluation datasets may contain sensitive data; apply access control and minimization.
Tool simulators must model authorization and side effects accurately enough for the tested property.
Judge model output is untrusted evidence and cannot override deterministic safety assertions.
Trace exports are redacted before leaving the trusted runtime.
Production release gate consumes immutable run metadata and dataset/config hashes.
failurePaths: Dataset drift: fingerprint dataset and rerun baseline on new version.
Judge disagreement: route to human review and calibrate judge thresholds.
Rare safety regression: inspect adversarial slices and enforce hard gates.
Trace contains secrets: redact and block export.
Candidate overfits benchmark: maintain held-out cases and rotate adversarial examples.
Metric improves but task success falls: inspect per-dimension metrics and do not rely on aggregate alone.

workedExample.problem: Decide whether a refund support agent is eligible for release after a 100-case evaluation.
workedExample.input: task_success=92%; tool_accuracy=96%; groundedness=88%; safety_failures=1 cross-tenant event; p95=1800ms; cost/task=$0.012.

steps.reasoning: 92 of 100 cases meet expected final behavior.
96 cases use expected tools; 88 include required source support.
One trace attempted a cross-tenant lookup, which is a critical hard-gate failure.
p95 latency and cost are within configured limits, but cannot compensate for a safety failure.
Fix tenant isolation, add regression coverage and rerun the pinned dataset before canary.

workedExample.expectedOutput: Candidate is rejected because a critical tenant-isolation gate failed, despite acceptable task quality and runtime metrics.

implementations.expectedResult: Deterministic task, tool, citation, trajectory, safety, latency and cost metrics with aggregate rates.
SQLite ledger fingerprints dataset/config, pins candidate metadata and stores idempotent per-case evaluation results.

failures.name: Only final answer evaluated
failures.symptom: Agent gets a high score despite using unauthorized tools or inventing evidence.
failures.rootCause: Evaluation checks prose but ignores trajectory and side effects.
failures.recovery: Score tool calls, arguments, citations, state transitions and safety alongside final output.
failures.regressionTest: Add a case with correct answer text but forbidden tool call; assert hard-gate failure.

failures.name: Benchmark leakage
failures.symptom: Prompt is tuned until golden cases pass but fails on unseen requests.
failures.rootCause: Development examples and held-out evaluation set are mixed.
failures.recovery: Version train/dev/test splits and preserve adversarial holdouts.
failures.regressionTest: Run candidate against an unseen holdout slice before release.

failures.name: Judge model false pass
failures.symptom: LLM judge approves an unsupported answer or misses a policy violation.
failures.rootCause: Judge shares model blind spots and replaces deterministic assertions.
failures.recovery: Use deterministic safety checks and calibrate subjective judges against human labels.
failures.regressionTest: Inject a known citation mismatch and assert deterministic validator rejects it.

failures.name: Aggregate hides rare severe failure
failures.symptom: 99% success masks one cross-tenant data leak.
failures.recovery: Make security properties non-compensable hard gates and report slice metrics.
failures.regressionTest: Any cross-tenant event forces release eligibility false.

failures.name: Unreproducible run
failures.symptom: Results cannot be recreated after prompt or model changes.
failures.rootCause: Dataset, candidate, tool schema or config version not recorded.
failures.recovery: Persist fingerprints and pinned version metadata with every run.
failures.regressionTest: Reopen ledger and assert dataset/config hashes and candidate version remain identical.

scenarioQuiz.question: An agent has 99% task success but one cross-tenant data leak. Can it ship?
options: No, critical safety hard gate fails
Only if model confidence is high
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Critical security failures are non-compensable and block release regardless of aggregate quality.

scenarioQuiz.question: What should a trajectory evaluation inspect?
options: Decisions, tool calls, arguments, observations, state transitions and stop behavior
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Agent failures often occur in the path, not just the final text.

scenarioQuiz.question: Why pin dataset and configuration hashes?
options: To reproduce and compare runs fairly
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Fingerprints identify the exact data and configuration behind an evaluation result.

scenarioQuiz.question: What is the role of an LLM judge?
options: Assist subjective evaluation after calibration against human labels
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Judges can help with subjective quality but must be calibrated and cannot replace deterministic safety checks.

Evaluation metadata can be reopened and reproduced.
